done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `PERIOD_WORD_PATTERN` treats the bare word `quarter` as a named period, although `parseNamedTimeWindow` can resolve only a numbered/ordinal quarter. For a common no-period question such as “Show Actual by quarter,” both parsers return null, but `hasTimePeriodWords` returns true, so the model-emitted window is neither cleared nor replaced by the prior window. The answer can therefore use an arbitrary model period instead of aggregating or inheriting as required. The table-driven test covers “by month” but omits the equivalent “by quarter” case.
findings.title: Not done: A no-period “by quarter” question can preserve the model’s window

findings.body: The amount disambiguation does not recognize the standalone `=` operator. For example, “Show Actual = 2025” reaches `calendarYear`; its prefix ends in `=`, which does not match `[<>]=?`, so the code returns 2025 and overrides the model or inherited window with the full 2025 calendar year. This is an unambiguous amount comparison and violates the requirement that an amount is never read as a year. The added cases test word-form comparisons but omit this operator.
findings.title: Not done: An amount can still be read as a calendar year

findings.body: The previous test-coverage gap remains open. The new regression matrix calls `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose provider, executor/database, audit, dimensions, and selection resolver are fakes. Frontend Ask tests mock the API, and the repository test command contains no Playwright/browser suite or Playwright specification. Thus named-period follow-ups, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and period-control reruns are still not proven through the required browser, running API, and real database boundary; the successful close run only establishes the hermetic tests.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
